question: Should five consecutive malformed Google Meet pullAudio payloads terminate the active bridge under the existing input-error cutoff?
rationale: The code can safely reject malformed bytes either way, but whether repeated protocol corruption should close the session or be dropped indefinitely is an availability policy choice not settled by tests or contributor proof.

options.title: Keep the five-error cutoff
options.body: Treat malformed payloads like other repeated input failures so a persistently broken node bridge closes and can be recovered rather than remaining silently unusable.

options.title: Reject without consuming the cutoff
options.body: Drop malformed chunks while keeping the bridge alive, reducing outage risk but allowing a permanently corrupted source to remain connected and silent.

recommendation.title: Keep the five-error cutoff
recommendation.body: Treat malformed payloads like other repeated input failures so a persistently broken node bridge closes and can be recovered rather than remaining silently unusable.

likelyOwner.reason: They merged the related cutoff behavior and were explicitly mentioned for the current availability-risk review.
